# Build Process Runs

Process runs instantiate a process template, assign resources to its slots, and
record step parameters for one execution.

## Define slots and steps

```python
from recap import Direction

with namespace.build_process_template("Measure Sample", "1.0") as template:
    template.add_resource_slot("sample", "sample", Direction.input)
    template.add_resource_slot("result", "file", Direction.output)
    (
        template.add_step("Measure")
        .add_parameters({
            "acquisition": [
                {"name": "exposure", "type": "float", "default": 1.0},
                {"name": "mode", "type": "str", "default": "standard"},
            ]
        })
        .bind_slot("source", "sample")
        .bind_slot("destination", "result")
        .close_step()
    )
```

Slots declare compatible resource types. Role bindings let a step refer to a
slot by purpose instead of by a concrete resource name.

## Create and assign a run

```python
with namespace.build_process_run(
    name="Run 001",
    description="Sample measurement",
    template_name="Measure Sample",
    version="1.0",
) as run:
    run.assign_resource("sample", sample_resource)
    run.assign_resource("result", result_resource)
```

The resulting ProcessRun records the template, assignments, ordered steps, and
parameter values. Use `process_run_id=` when updating a known run to avoid a
name-based lookup.

## Resources must be visible from the run's namespace

A slot resource must belong to the run's namespace or one of its ancestors.
Resources in sibling, descendant, or unrelated namespaces are rejected when
the run is saved. Having permission to read another namespace does not bypass
this visibility rule.

To explicitly copy a resource from another namespace into the run's namespace:

```python
with namespace.build_process_run(
    "Run 002", "Copied sample measurement", "Measure Sample", "1.0"
) as builder:
    builder.assign_resource("sample", other_sample, copy=True)

assigned_copy = builder.process_run.assigned_resources["sample"].resource
```

Only graph roots can be copied; the entire tree is copied with fresh IDs and
`copied_from_id` pointing to the source root. The saved assignment therefore
has a different resource ID. Values and metadata are copied independently.
Child-step references to nodes of the original tree are remapped onto the
matching nodes of the assigned copy, separately for each slot.

Copying requires read access to the source namespace and resource-write access
to the run's namespace, in addition to permission to create or update the run.
Copy and assignment commit or roll back together. Archived sources may be copied;
the new resource is mutable. If the resource is already visible, `copy=True`
uses the original instead of creating an unnecessary copy.

Before save, the builder's assignment still refers to the source. Read the
persisted resource from `builder.process_run` after save. A later plain
`assign_resource()` call for the same slot clears its pending copy opt-in.

When copying a process run to another namespace, carried assignments must also
be visible there. Replace a non-visible slot explicitly with
`ProcessRunCopyOptions(changes=ProcessRunCopyChanges(assignments={"sample": resource.id},
copy_assignments=("sample",)))` to copy its resource and preserve child refinements.

## Record dynamic resources

When an experiment discovers resource structure at runtime, add child resources
through a resource builder. Process-run builders can add named runtime children
beneath template-generated steps. Children reuse the parent's step template,
start with template defaults, and inherit run resources by role. See
[Add Runtime Children](add-runtime-children.qmd) for creation and nested access.

## Set generated process parameters

Generated parameter models provide typed access to values declared by a process
step. Read model, mutate it, then submit it back to run:

```python
with namespace.build_process_run(process_run_id=run.id) as builder:
    params = builder.get_params("Measure")
    params.acquisition.exposure = 2.5
    params.acquisition.mode = "fast"
    builder.set_params(params)
```

`set_params()` flushes updated values as part of builder transaction.

## Finalize a completed run

Finalize is separate lifecycle action. Call it after assignments, steps, and
parameters are complete:

```python
with namespace.build_process_run(process_run_id=run.id) as builder:
    builder.finalize()
```

Finalization marks run active.

## Archive a run

Archive completed runs separately when they should remain queryable but no longer
be treated as active:

```python
with namespace.build_process_run(process_run_id=run.id) as builder:
    builder.archive()
```
